As Council will know, based on the point in time count, conducted in October 2024, the number of people experiencing homelessness and housing instability in our city has tripled between 2022 and 2024. Prior to that, the number had also doubled between 2008 and 2022.

We have a range of programs across multiple departments that aim to assist low-income residents with improved access to services, supporting community organizations in providing services, connecting people through programs and access to civic services.
We also have initiatives that focus on longer-term systemic pieces such as increasing the inventory of affordable housing.
We work with partners that build and operate new housing units in order to add new transition on supportive housing units to our inventory in the city.

We're also working on the development of a community well-being framework to focus on areas of prevention and upstream action to improve quality of life and equitable access to services for our residents.

In addition, we've been working with partners on development of the Saskatoon homelessness action plan, and with federal funding, we've been working to implement the city's community encampment response plan, which includes new housing units and supportive facilities.
In addition to these programs and strategies, our emergency response efforts have also been a critical component and are coordinated among various departments in the city.

This includes the encampment cleanup responses, working with community partners, working with people in encampments to connect them to services, overdose outreach teams, and addressing safety issues and shared in public spaces.

We've also been involved in ongoing efforts to secure locations for warming and cooling locations, improving drinking water and washroom access and other efforts, which have had various reports to council over the past months.
This report also provides preliminary information related to our estimated costs for 2024 encampment cleanups, which was approximately $600,000.
We're continuing to work across departments to further identify and track direct costs as well as service impacts due to increasing responses required to address the challenges in our community.
